title: Legal Expertise: A Documentary Record of Arbitrariness
subtitle: This is not a dispute over interpretations; it is the documentation of a collapse of the rule of law. Investigative records read in defiance of their text, and the systematic disregard for final judicial acts.
intro: This section provides a rigorous legal analysis exposing the mechanics of fabrication in the Lagovsky case. We demonstrate the systematic violation of the principle of res judicata (the finality of binding court rulings) and the intentional subversion of meaning in investigative protocols. When a lawyer's lawful commercial activity is recategorised as a crime in direct contradiction to Supreme Court rulings, the very foundation of justice is destroyed.

sections.title: Defence Line in the Republic of Serbia
sections.content: Procedural memoranda establishing the civil and commercial nature of the dispute.
sections.summary: The defence has consistently established that the extradition request is legally void, as it is based on a transaction whose lawfulness was upheld by the highest Russian arbitration courts. This acts as a fundamental barrier against the criminalisation of law.

sections.title: International Human Rights Standard
sections.content: Case assessment by independent institutions under Articles 6 and 18 ECHR.
sections.summary: Characterisation of the prosecution as politically and economically motivated. International observers document the use of the criminal justice system as leverage in a private corporate conflict, a practice incompatible with the rule of law.

sections.title: Expert Review: The Destruction of Legal Certainty
sections.content: Memoranda by international law practitioners on the absence of a criminal offence.
sections.summary: A detailed analysis of how the investigation ignores judicial finality. Experts emphasise that if a lawyer's professional opinion on market value constitutes a crime, the legal profession itself ceases to have any meaning.

sections.title: Documentary Inversion: Investigation vs Facts
sections.content: An analysis of inspection records where the investigators' conclusions directly contradict the texts recorded within them. This provides irrefutable evidence of the intentional falsification of meaning.

episodes.label: Requiring 'Real Value' Framed as 'Criminal Intent'
episodes.what_protocol_says: CRM correspondence dated 01.12.2021: Dmitry Lagovsky writes — 'the value must be real'. The investigators (protocol dated 17.12.2022) quote this as proof of a conspiracy to suppress the price.
episodes.what_it_actually_means: This is a legal absurdity. 'Real value' is synonymous with fair market price. A person planning a fraud requests a 'lower figure'. A demand for price reality is direct evidence of good faith, which the investigation intentionally interprets in the opposite sense.

episodes.label: Routine Professional Travel Framed as 'Criminal Activity'
episodes.what_protocol_says: The investigation labels a trip to collect a hard copy of a report on 14.07.2021 as 'illogical', citing it as proof of criminal intent.
episodes.what_it_actually_means: The same CRM records confirm: the report was sent by post, but the lawyer required a physical copy for his files. A routine office task is labeled 'illogical' solely to artificially construct a criminal narrative where none exists.

episodes.label: Technical Confirmation 'Sent in PDF' Framed as 'Proof of Conspiracy'
episodes.what_protocol_says: The phrase 'Ira, thanks, sent in PDF' by an appraisal firm employee is included as evidence that 'the appraisers agreed to suppress the value'.
episodes.what_it_actually_means: This is a prime example of the total degradation of the evidentiary threshold. A standard workplace confirmation of a file transfer is presented as a sign of criminal conspiracy. The text contains no mention of price or illegal acts — only the technical recording of a document being sent.

sections.summary: Each episode proves one point: the investigation is not making 'errors'; it is systematically distorting the meaning of documents to create the appearance of a crime in perfectly lawful acts. This is textbook fabrication.

summary: The legal position rests on the inviolability of judicial acts (res judicata) and the prohibition on prosecuting a lawyer for his professional conduct. The documents confirm: this is not a criminal case, but an act of extra-judicial pressure.

theses.title: Assault on Legal Independence: A Precedent of Arbitrariness
theses.text: The criminal prosecution of Dmitry Lagovsky for providing legal counsel is a direct assault on the independence of the profession. Under the UN Basic Principles (1990), lawyers must not be identified with their clients. Seeking to extradite a lawyer for advice on market value compliance shatters the principle of legal certainty. If this request is granted, no lawyer in the world can feel safe while performing their professional duties.

sources.label: UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers (Havana, 1990)

theses.title: Criminalising a Lost Arbitration
theses.text: This is an attempt to 'replay' final arbitration rulings through the power of the criminal justice apparatus. When a minority shareholder loses all commercial litigation, he initiates a criminal case, using the lawyer as a 'tool of procedural pressure'. The failure of Serbian courts to respect the acts of the Russian Supreme Court upholding the transaction is an abandonment of the basic principle of international comity and the filtering of arbitrariness.

sources.label: Russian Supreme Court ruling on the lawfulness of the transaction (PDF)

theses.title: Violation of Proportionality (Articles 5 & 6 ECHR)
theses.text: The requesting state seeks the extradition of a legal consultant for detention in a case where the organizers and company heads have already received symbolic suspended sentences. The demand for actual imprisonment for an external consultant is an act of blatant injustice and disproportionality, expressly forbidden by European human rights standards.
